# API and data — the rules in force

Loaded with `apps/api`, `packages/contracts`, `packages/db`, `packages/crypto`, `packages/logger`. Each line names the record it comes from; open that record when the line is not enough. Which windows are open and which records are in force is stated once, in [the ledger](../plan/README.md#the-window).

- **Functional style, no OOP** — No `class`, no `this`, no decorators, no DI framework. Every layer is `create<Module><Layer>(deps)` returning an `as const` object; types come from `ReturnType`. Third-party constructors are wrapped in `create*` functions. — [ADR-0009](../adr/0009-api-modular-layering.md) (modular API)
- **Layers** — `*.routes.ts` → `*.controller.ts` → `*.service.ts` → `*.repository.ts`. Services never import Express or SQL; repositories hold every Drizzle query; controllers read `req.valid`, call the service with `req.ctx` first, and answer through `respond.*`. — [ADR-0009](../adr/0009-api-modular-layering.md) (modular API)
- **Envelope** — Controllers use `respond.ok / created / list / noContent` and nothing else; `res.json` appears only inside the API's own `core/http`. — [ADR-0012](../adr/0012-response-envelope.md) (unified response envelope)
- **Errors** — One branded `AppError`, thrown through factories (`notFound()`, `forbidden()`, a module's `*.errors.ts`) and matched with `isAppError(e)` plus `e.code` — never `instanceof`, never a new error class. The API's `message` is developer-facing English and is never rendered by a client. The handler reports 5xx through the reporting seam and the response shape does not widen. — [ADR-0013](../adr/0013-error-model.md) (error model and HTTP status mapping) as carried by [ADR-0066](../adr/0066-infrastructure-seams.md)
- **Configuration** — In `apps/api/src` only `core/config` reads `process.env`; in `@repo/db` only `src/tooling/env.ts` does. A new variable means a zod schema entry, an `.env.example` line and — when a task reads it — a `turbo.json` `env` entry. — [ADR-0004](../adr/0004-configuration-and-environment.md) (configuration and environment validation) as carried by [ADR-0059](../adr/0059-ci-containers-and-deployment.md) and [ADR-0075](../adr/0075-loading-environment-files.md) and [ADR-0081](../adr/0081-build-versions.md)
- **Build versions** — Two facts name a build, under the same two names in every Dockerfile, in compose and in `turbo.json`: `APP_VERSION`, the release label, one value for the whole product and never parsed, and `GIT_SHA`, the commit. Both are stamped at image build as build arguments — never passed to a running container, never read from a `package.json`. Unset, the label is `dev` and the commit is absent, and an empty string is unset. `/health` answers them as `version` and `commit`, its shape unchanged. — [ADR-0081](../adr/0081-build-versions.md) (build versions), [ADR-0004](../adr/0004-configuration-and-environment.md) (configuration and environment validation) as carried by [ADR-0059](../adr/0059-ci-containers-and-deployment.md) and [ADR-0075](../adr/0075-loading-environment-files.md) and [ADR-0081](../adr/0081-build-versions.md), [ADR-0016](../adr/0016-health-checks.md) (health check endpoints) as carried by [ADR-0066](../adr/0066-infrastructure-seams.md) and [ADR-0081](../adr/0081-build-versions.md)
- **Loading env files** — An env file is loaded with Node's own loader (`--env-file`, `process.loadEnvFile`): the environment wins over the file, and a missing file is skipped. No file in the API image's `dist/` carries a loader package; a test harness may keep one as a dev dependency when it must override. Beside the application — harnesses, the browser tier, repository scripts — a process may read what it needs and forwards it unvalidated; a real configuration surface goes behind a schema. `@repo/db`'s CLI tooling may read an unset `NODE_ENV` as `development`; the API requires it. — [ADR-0075](../adr/0075-loading-environment-files.md) (loading environment files)
- **Request context** — Services take `ctx: RequestContext` as their first parameter; `getContext()` belongs to infrastructure only. — [ADR-0010](../adr/0010-request-context.md) (request context object and propagation)
- **Validation** — Zod schemas live in `@repo/contracts` and are re-exported by `<module>.schemas.ts`; controllers read `req.valid.{params,query,body}` and nothing else; bodies are `.strict()`. — [ADR-0011](../adr/0011-middleware-pipeline.md) (middleware pipeline), [ADR-0023](../adr/0023-shared-contracts-package.md) (shared contracts package)
- **Auth and guards** — Two populations — `staff` and `user` — with separate tables and separate segments `/api/v1/{public,user,admin}`; `authenticate()` at router level and `authorize()` at the mount; `super_admin` bypasses staff role checks. Self-scoped resources carry no `authorize` because the subject is `ctx.principal`. An impersonated session is a `user` session minted by staff: it carries the actor, rotates without extending, and refuses credential operations. — [ADR-0017](../adr/0017-identity-model-populations-and-roles.md) (identity model) as carried by [ADR-0067](../adr/0067-organizations.md) and [ADR-0071](../adr/0071-mail-flows.md) and [ADR-0072](../adr/0072-federated-identity-google-sign-in.md), [ADR-0019](../adr/0019-authorization-guards.md) (authorization guards) as carried by [ADR-0067](../adr/0067-organizations.md), [ADR-0057](../adr/0057-impersonation-sessions.md) (impersonation sessions) as carried by [ADR-0067](../adr/0067-organizations.md) and [ADR-0070](../adr/0070-impersonation-in-a-new-tab.md) and [ADR-0071](../adr/0071-mail-flows.md) and [ADR-0072](../adr/0072-federated-identity-google-sign-in.md)
- **The key ring** — The access token is signed under `JWT_ACCESS_SECRET` and names it in a `kid` header; `JWT_ACCESS_SECRET_PREVIOUS`, when set, is verified for tokens that name it and never signs, a `kid` naming neither is refused, and a token with no `kid` verifies under the current secret alone. The OIDC transaction codec signs under `OIDC_TRANSACTION_SECRET`, or a key derived from the access secret under a label of its own when unset, and never under the access key. A committed value is refused in production for every secret. — [ADR-0078](../adr/0078-backend-closing-wave.md) (backend closing wave) as carried by [ADR-0083](../adr/0083-row-level-security-without-widenings.md)
- **Database** — Schema in `packages/db/src/schema`; migrations are generated with `drizzle-kit generate` and committed, never pushed; the API never auto-migrates; seeds are idempotent. The API connects as the application role (`DATABASE_URL`) with table privileges and no DDL, and every tooling connection is the owner role (`DATABASE_URL_OWNER`, required with no fallback). — [ADR-0006](../adr/0006-database-postgres-drizzle.md) (postgreSQL with Drizzle ORM in a shared `@repo/db` package) as carried by [ADR-0061](../adr/0061-database-roles-and-append-only-enforcement.md) and [ADR-0073](../adr/0073-review-hardening.md), [ADR-0008](../adr/0008-database-migrations-and-seeding.md) (database migrations, setup and seeding) as carried by [ADR-0059](../adr/0059-ci-containers-and-deployment.md) and [ADR-0078](../adr/0078-backend-closing-wave.md) and [ADR-0061](../adr/0061-database-roles-and-append-only-enforcement.md), [ADR-0061](../adr/0061-database-roles-and-append-only-enforcement.md) (database roles and append-only enforcement)
- **Migrations applied by hash** — `db:migrate` is the repository's own runner, under the advisory lock: a journal entry is applied when no row of `drizzle.__drizzle_migrations` records its hash or its journal timestamp — never because it is newer than the newest row — in journal order, a run of ordinary files in one transaction. A file whose first line is `-- migrate:concurrently` runs each statement on its own outside any transaction and is recorded when the last succeeds, so its statements are single and repeatable (an index is dropped `CONCURRENTLY IF EXISTS` before it is built). The migrations directory is pinned to LF. — [ADR-0078](../adr/0078-backend-closing-wave.md) (backend closing wave) as carried by [ADR-0083](../adr/0083-row-level-security-without-widenings.md)
- **Append-only audit** — `audit_events` is append-only in the database as well as in the lint rule — a revoked grant and a `BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE` trigger — so retention is a reviewed migration and never a job. — [ADR-0058](../adr/0058-append-only-audit-log.md) (an append-only audit log) as carried by [ADR-0061](../adr/0061-database-roles-and-append-only-enforcement.md), [ADR-0061](../adr/0061-database-roles-and-append-only-enforcement.md) (database roles and append-only enforcement)
- **Per-population data** — Per-population data gets a table per population with a real foreign key rather than a discriminated table; `sessions` is the single exception and says why in place. — [ADR-0045](../adr/0045-user-settings.md) (user settings) as carried by [ADR-0053](../adr/0053-account-area.md) and [ADR-0077](../adr/0077-shared-composition-second-wave.md), [ADR-0053](../adr/0053-account-area.md) (the account area) as carried by [ADR-0077](../adr/0077-shared-composition-second-wave.md)
- **List endpoints at scale** — One list-query language, its codec in `@repo/contracts`. `offset` has a ceiling and `count` is an optional flag: with `count=false` a repository skips the aggregate and returns `total: null`. Every sortable and searched column carries a covering index declaration, trigram indexes for search and btree for sorts. — [ADR-0014](../adr/0014-pagination-filtering-sorting.md) (pagination, filtering and sorting conventions) as carried by [ADR-0060](../adr/0060-list-endpoints-at-scale.md), [ADR-0060](../adr/0060-list-endpoints-at-scale.md) (list endpoints at scale) as carried by [ADR-0078](../adr/0078-backend-closing-wave.md)
- **Tenancy** — One database, one schema: every tenant-owned table carries `organization_id not null` and is indexed tenant-led, with no bare `(column, id)` pairs beside those composites. A repository over such a table takes the organization id as a required parameter; the sanctioned exception is a read scoped by the **principal** rather than by a tenant, named in its repository for what it is, and the hand-maintained `TENANT_OWNED_TABLES` list is what the enumeration test checks the roster against. Every path that creates a user creates their personal organization in the same transaction, and every path that deletes one soft-deletes it in the same transaction; staff are never members. A third guard, `requireMembership(...roles)`, resolves the caller's membership of the organization in the path and places it on the context — a non-member is answered `404` rather than `403`, a member whose role is too low `403`, and only the guard that checks writes the field. The `/user` segment's organization requests carry `/orgs/:orgId`; requests about the caller — their organizations, their invitations — stay outside it. Impersonated sessions are refused the tenant writes: role changes, removals and leaving, deletion, and creating or accepting an invitation. An invitation names an address, not an account: its create path mints a single-use token and stores only the SHA-256 in `token_hash`, which nothing returns and nothing reads until the mail deliverable — acceptance in D15 matches by address. — [ADR-0067](../adr/0067-organizations.md) (organizations) as carried by [ADR-0078](../adr/0078-backend-closing-wave.md)
- **Row-level security** — Every table in `TENANT_OWNED_TABLES` declares a `pgPolicy` per setting that may admit a row — `app.organization_id` (read and write), `app.user_id` (a user's own memberships and the invitations addressed to them: read, and an invitation stamped, never a membership written), `app.invitation_token_hash` (read and an accept stamped) — and the application role sees nothing a placed setting does not name. No setting widens anything: whatever must see every tenant connects as the owner. The invitee's and the bearer's consume policies admit only an unended invitation and check the row they leave: an invitee never revokes, a bearer only accepts, neither clears a stamp, and an invitation carries at most one terminal stamp. The root's transaction helper places the request's scope on every transaction it opens and clears every setting that scope does not name (`openInRequestScope`, from the context `authenticate`, `requireMembership` and `placeRouteOrganization` filled — once an organization is placed, the principal is not). Staff hold no widening: a route under `/admin/organizations/:id` places its organization through `placeRouteOrganization`, a staff request places nothing else, so a staff read that names no organization reads no tenant-owned row, and a foreign key's cascade needs no setting; row-level security defends against a forgotten predicate, not injection, and the scope stays in request storage, held there by a concurrency test; a tenant-owned repository runs on its caller's transaction or opens one the same way (`withinTransaction`), never on the bare pool. A path that creates or joins an organization places it (`memberships.enterOrganization`) before writing a membership; the seeders connect as the owner, and a test reads across tenants through `asOwner` alone. The application role may update an invitation's stamps and no other column, and in production the API refuses to start as a superuser, a `BYPASSRLS` role, a member of either, the owner of any table, or a role its login switched to, and refuses a `DATABASE_URL` whose password the repository commits or that carries none, and the migrate job refuses the same of `DATABASE_URL_OWNER`. The tenant-owned tables carry exactly the declared policies, roles, `USING` and `WITH CHECK` included; no view reads one without `security_invoker`, and no `SECURITY DEFINER` function or rewrite rule other than a view's own exists outside the system schemas, each held by a schema test. A staff surface over tenant rows outside `/admin/organizations/:id` names its organization or takes a record of its own, never a widening. — [ADR-0083](../adr/0083-row-level-security-without-widenings.md) (row-level security without widenings), [ADR-0078](../adr/0078-backend-closing-wave.md) (backend closing wave) as carried by [ADR-0083](../adr/0083-row-level-security-without-widenings.md), [ADR-0067](../adr/0067-organizations.md) (organizations) as carried by [ADR-0078](../adr/0078-backend-closing-wave.md)
- **Infrastructure seams** — Mail goes through the `MailSender` port in `core/mail` and never through a client a service imports; `GET /metrics` lives in `core/metrics` beside `/health`, above every limiter, labelled by route pattern and behind a token; the reporter in `core/reporting` fires on 5xx only and is given the request id, route, status and principal — never the body; every rate limiter shares one store, Redis when configured and memory otherwise, failing closed. All four seams are inert in a default clone. — [ADR-0066](../adr/0066-infrastructure-seams.md) (infrastructure seams)
- **The development rate-limit profile** — The committed development template, `.env.example`, raises `RATE_LIMIT_GLOBAL_MAX` to hold a failed verification run and its retry; the schema default stays the security baseline's number, and the production template does not carry the variable, so a deployment that states nothing inherits the baseline. A development value is kept off the deployment's path by separation, not refused at startup. — [ADR-0069](../adr/0069-development-rate-limit-profile.md) (the development rate-limit profile)
- **A per-principal hash budget** — Every authenticated route that verifies a password through the hash limiter also carries the per-principal limiter, keyed on `ctx.principal.id` (`RATE_LIMIT_PRINCIPAL_HASH_MAX` per `RATE_LIMIT_PRINCIPAL_HASH_WINDOW`), so a few sessions cannot shed login for everyone and an actor guessing their own password spends their own budget. The rule is the criterion — a new route that verifies a password joins it — and the roster lives in the specs and the integration tier. — [ADR-0073](../adr/0073-review-hardening.md) (review hardening) as carried by [ADR-0074](../adr/0074-review-follow-ups.md) and [ADR-0076](../adr/0076-the-native-compiler.md) and [ADR-0078](../adr/0078-backend-closing-wave.md)
- **Limiter keys** — A limiter key never degrades to one shared bucket: without a validated address the key generator falls back to the socket's remote address and warns once per process naming the proxy configuration. The fallback keys the limiter only and is never written to `sessions.ip`. — [ADR-0073](../adr/0073-review-hardening.md) (review hardening) as carried by [ADR-0074](../adr/0074-review-follow-ups.md) and [ADR-0076](../adr/0076-the-native-compiler.md) and [ADR-0078](../adr/0078-backend-closing-wave.md)
- **The session cap and the prune** — Login and the federated exchange revoke the principal's oldest live sessions beyond `AUTH_MAX_SESSIONS_PER_PRINCIPAL` (`0` uncapped) inside the mint's transaction, reason `session_cap`. An impersonated session neither counts toward the cap nor is evicted by it — it ends on its own clock. The reference deployment runs the `prune` service on `PRUNE_INTERVAL`, so a production database stops growing by default. — [ADR-0073](../adr/0073-review-hardening.md) (review hardening) as carried by [ADR-0074](../adr/0074-review-follow-ups.md) and [ADR-0076](../adr/0076-the-native-compiler.md) and [ADR-0078](../adr/0078-backend-closing-wave.md), [ADR-0074](../adr/0074-review-follow-ups.md) (review follow-ups)
- **Credential events spend every link** — One `supersedeAll(ctx, principal, tx)` in `core/tokens` spends every outstanding account link, and every credential event calls it — an administrative or staff reset, a password or address change, an account deletion — rather than a per-purpose loop copied into a service. A purpose that should survive a credential event says so where it is declared. — [ADR-0074](../adr/0074-review-follow-ups.md) (review follow-ups), [ADR-0071](../adr/0071-mail-flows.md) (mail flows) as carried by [ADR-0072](../adr/0072-federated-identity-google-sign-in.md) and [ADR-0073](../adr/0073-review-hardening.md) and [ADR-0074](../adr/0074-review-follow-ups.md)
- **Lock order, and the deadlock retry** — A credential event sweeps its token rows under the principal's credential lock (`supersedeAll` takes it after the `reset_password` rows) and then locks the account; the federated exchange takes the same lock, then the account row, then claims its handoff, and the Google callback takes it before the account row it mints behind — so none holds what another waits for. The composition root's transaction helper runs a deadlock victim (`40P01`) again, three runs in all, logging each retry, and passes every other failure through at once; nothing inside a transaction has an effect outside the database, which is what makes that safe. — [ADR-0078](../adr/0078-backend-closing-wave.md) (backend closing wave) as carried by [ADR-0083](../adr/0083-row-level-security-without-widenings.md)
- **The impersonation exchange ends what it replaces** — When `POST /user/auth/impersonate` arrives with a refresh cookie that resolves to a live impersonated session, the exchange revokes that session and writes its `impersonation.ended` row, marked replaced, in the transaction that mints the new one. A cookie resolving to a real customer session is left alive in the database, and one resolving to nothing is ignored. — [ADR-0070](../adr/0070-impersonation-in-a-new-tab.md) (impersonation opens the customer app in a new tab)
- **Account deletion** — A user is soft-deleted — `deleted_at`, `status = 'disabled'`, every live session revoked `account_deleted` and every federated identity hard-deleted, in one transaction — and the address is released by a partial unique index, so every `on conflict` on `users.email`, seeds included, carries the `deleted_at is null` predicate. A deleted account stays readable and refuses writes with `409 USER_DELETED`; there is no restore. Staff are hard-deleted, never by themselves, under the rank rule and the last-super-admin invariant behind its advisory lock, their sessions revoked before the row goes. — [ADR-0028](../adr/0028-account-deletion.md) (account deletion), [ADR-0072](../adr/0072-federated-identity-google-sign-in.md) (federated identity) as carried by [ADR-0078](../adr/0078-backend-closing-wave.md)
- **Federated identity** — A sign-in resolves by `(provider, subject)` first and by address only when the claim is verified, the provider is authoritative for the address, and a live `active` user holds it. The Google routes mount only when both client settings are set; the provider is a port with a fake the integration tier drives. The callback hands off through a sixty-second `federated_login` account token bound to the browser the callback answered, and a password written without the account's own authority removes every federated identity. Link and unlink are refused to an impersonated session, and unlinking the last credential is refused. — [ADR-0072](../adr/0072-federated-identity-google-sign-in.md) (federated identity) as carried by [ADR-0078](../adr/0078-backend-closing-wave.md)
- **Server timeouts and the runtime floor** — `server.ts` sets the request, headers and keep-alive timeouts from `HTTP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT`, `HTTP_HEADERS_TIMEOUT` and `HTTP_KEEP_ALIVE_TIMEOUT` beside the drain deadline, keep-alive above a proxy's. The runtime floor is Node 24 at the patch the dependency tree requires (`engines.node`), with `.nvmrc`, the workflows and the Dockerfiles moving together; pnpm 12 through Corepack, its settings in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. — [ADR-0073](../adr/0073-review-hardening.md) (review hardening) as carried by [ADR-0074](../adr/0074-review-follow-ups.md) and [ADR-0076](../adr/0076-the-native-compiler.md) and [ADR-0078](../adr/0078-backend-closing-wave.md)
- **Invariants in the database** — `updated_at` is written by the column's `$onUpdate`, not by a repository remembering it, and `users` carries `CHECK (status <> 'active' OR email_verified_at IS NOT NULL)` — an invariant the code leans on is a database error, not a review finding. — [ADR-0073](../adr/0073-review-hardening.md) (review hardening) as carried by [ADR-0074](../adr/0074-review-follow-ups.md) and [ADR-0076](../adr/0076-the-native-compiler.md) and [ADR-0078](../adr/0078-backend-closing-wave.md)
- **The composition root and the line ceiling** — `core/container.ts` is ordering only: `createRateLimiters(config, store)` returns the named set and each module exports one `wire<Module>(deps)` returning its repositories, services and controllers. No source file in the trees the hygiene test's `LINE_CEILING_ROOTS` names — the API's modules and `core` among them — runs past a thousand lines. — [ADR-0073](../adr/0073-review-hardening.md) (review hardening) as carried by [ADR-0074](../adr/0074-review-follow-ups.md) and [ADR-0076](../adr/0076-the-native-compiler.md) and [ADR-0078](../adr/0078-backend-closing-wave.md), [ADR-0074](../adr/0074-review-follow-ups.md) (review follow-ups)
- **Logging** — pino through `ctx.logger`; a fields object first and a short static message second; no `console.*`. — [ADR-0005](../adr/0005-logging.md) (structured logging with pino)
- **Contracts** — `@repo/contracts` depends on `zod` alone; an enum is defined there once and consumed by both `pgEnum` and zod. — [ADR-0023](../adr/0023-shared-contracts-package.md) (shared contracts package)
- **Tests** — Unit tests use fake repositories as plain objects; integration tests go through `createApp(buildContainer({ db: testDb }))` and supertest against the test database. Every new endpoint gets both, plus a Postman request. — [ADR-0021](../adr/0021-testing-strategy.md) (testing strategy)
- **Lint is the mechanical half** — `packages/config-eslint/api.js` already fails the build on classes, raw responses, `process.env` and layer-crossing imports. A rule a reviewer keeps repeating belongs there instead. — [ADR-0002](../adr/0002-monorepo-layout-and-tooling.md) (monorepo layout and tooling) as carried by [ADR-0062](../adr/0062-frontend-build-and-shared-composition.md) and [ADR-0073](../adr/0073-review-hardening.md), [ADR-0062](../adr/0062-frontend-build-and-shared-composition.md) (frontend build and shared app composition) as carried by [ADR-0073](../adr/0073-review-hardening.md) and [ADR-0076](../adr/0076-the-native-compiler.md) and [ADR-0077](../adr/0077-shared-composition-second-wave.md)
- **Behaviour specs** — `docs/specs/<capability>.md` states what a client observes on the wire — requirements with WHEN/THEN scenarios, each citing its record and the test file that proves it — and is edited in place by the step that changes the behaviour, in the same diff as the code and the test. `pnpm docs:check` refuses a requirement without a scenario, a record that does not exist or a test that does not. — [ADR-0068](../adr/0068-behaviour-specs-and-plan-notes.md) (behaviour specs, and the plan apart from its notes)
